notices.trigger: Every home repair contract: the pamphlet is handed over; the signed Consumer Rights Acknowledgment Form is added when the contract is over $1,000
notices.support: For any contract for $1,000 or under, any person engaging in the business of home repair and remodeling shall provide to its customers a copy of the "Home Repair: Know Your Consumer Rights" pamphlet. No written acknowledgment of receipt of the pamphlet is required for a contract of $1,000 or under.
notices.summary_row: Pamphlet "Home Repair: Know Your Consumer Rights" (full text fixed by statute) and Consumer Rights Acknowledgment Form sentence
notices.block: 815 ILCS 513/20: pamphlet "Home Repair: Know Your Consumer Rights" and Consumer Rights Acknowledgment Form (full statutory pamphlet text)
notices.hold_reason: The only block is the whole section 513/20, with the duty and acknowledgment-form rules in (a) and (b) around the pamphlet, and the pamphlet must be a separate document; printing the block would put non-notice statute text in the contract.

notices.summary_row: Notice to owner (sworn statement), owner-occupied single-family
notices.block: 770 ILCS 60/5: sworn statement and notice to owner of owner-occupied single-family residence
notices.hold_reason: The only block is the whole section 770 ILCS 60/5, which includes the contractor's sworn-statement duty in (a) and other text around the notice in (b); printing the block would put non-notice statute text in the contract.

notices.trigger: Sale of $25 or more where the seller is physically present at the consumer's residence
notices.support: Floor: "$25 or more". Trigger: "seller who is physically present at the consumer's residence".
notices.summary_row: Three-day statement and NOTICE OF CANCELLATION form
notices.block: 815 ILCS 505/2B: home solicitation three-day cancellation (statement and NOTICE OF CANCELLATION form)
notices.hold_reason: The only block is the whole section 505/2B, with the unlawful-practice list and the exemptions around the statement and form; printing the block would put non-notice statute text in the contract.

notices.title: Arbitration clause and jury-waiver clause: consumer signs and writes "accept" or "reject" in the margin
notices.trigger: Contract contains a binding arbitration clause or a jury trial waiver
notices.format: Consumer signs and writes the word accept or reject in the margin next to each clause; otherwise the clause is null and void
notices.support: Any binding arbitration clause or jury trial waiver in a home repair contract needs the consumer's signature and the handwritten word "accept" or "reject" in the margin beside each clause, or the clause is null and void.
notices.summary_row: Arbitration and jury-waiver clauses: consumer signs and writes "accept" or "reject" in the margin
notices.block: 815 ILCS 513/15.1: arbitration and jury-waiver clauses need "accept" or "reject" in the margin
notices.hold_reason: no prescribed wording; the statute only lists required content

notices.title: Insurance-proceeds jobs: 10 point bold cancellation statement and duplicate NOTICE OF CANCELLATION
notices.trigger: Contract to be paid from the proceeds of a property and casualty insurance policy
notices.format: Statement in at least 10 point boldface; NOTICE OF CANCELLATION in duplicate, attached to the contract but easily detachable, boldface type of a minimum size of 10 points
notices.support: A contract to be paid from property insurance proceeds needs its own 10 point bold statement and a duplicate detachable NOTICE OF CANCELLATION
notices.summary_row: Insurance-proceeds jobs: 10 point bold statement plus duplicate NOTICE OF CANCELLATION; roofing license name and number on contracts
notices.block: 815 ILCS 513/18: insurance-proceeds jobs (statement and NOTICE OF CANCELLATION), roofing license line
notices.hold_reason: The only block is the whole section 513/18 (deductible rebate ban, roofing license, public adjuster and other rules around the notice); printing it would put non-notice statute text in the contract. Also the trigger depends on insurance payment, which the builder does not know.

changes.new: Over $1,000, furnished for signature before work starts; states total cost with parts and materials listed, any charge for an estimate, and the business name and address (815 ILCS 513/15)
changes.support: Prior to initiating home repair or remodeling work for over $1,000, a person engaged in the business of home repair or remodeling shall furnish to the customer for signature a written contract or work order that states the total cost, including parts and materials listed with reasonable particularity and any charge for an estimate. In addition, the contract shall state the business name and address of the person engaged in the business of home repair or remodeling.

changes.new: Three business days (815 ILCS 505/2B); age 65 or older with an uninvited solicitor, sold at the home: 15 full business days (815 ILCS 513/22)
changes.support: A person age 65 or older who purchases home repair or remodeling services from an uninvited solicitor may cancel any contract with a person engaged in home repair or remodeling by notifying that person within 15 full business days following the day on which the contract was signed if the agreement for the home repair or remodeling was made at the home of the purchaser.

changes.new: Age 65 or older, uninvited solicitor, agreement made at the purchaser's home: 15 full business days (815 ILCS 513/22). The 505/2B statement and form still say three business days.
changes.support: A person age 65 or older who purchases home repair or remodeling services from an uninvited solicitor may cancel any contract with a person engaged in home repair or remodeling by notifying that person within 15 full business days following the day on which the contract was signed if the agreement for the home repair or remodeling was made at the home of the purchaser.
in the same language as that used in the contract

changes.new: Disclosure in the contract and consent before charging; written notice 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline for terms of 12 months or more that renew for more than one month
changes.support: where such contract term is a specified term of 12 months or more, and where such contract automatically renews for a specified term of more than one month unless the consumer cancels the contract, shall notify the consumer in writing of the automatic renewal. Written notice shall be provided to the consumer no less than 30 days and no more than 60 days before the cancellation deadline

changes.new: OFFICIAL text read at ilga.gov; covers a written consumer contract that auto-renews; no small-business or service-type exemption
changes.support: No small-business or service-type exemption appears; exemptions are business-to-business contracts, banks, utilities under Article XXII, insurance-regulated parties.

unsure: IL-pamphlet: the pamphlet is a separate handout, not contract text, and the Attorney General's printed pamphlet differs from the statutory text; which to hand out is open.
IL-lien: it is unclear whether the notice should be printed in the contract or given as a separate statement before first payment; the statute allows either.
IL-arbitration-margin: no wording is prescribed, but the margin accept or reject mark is a signing step the contract may need to leave room for.
IL-insurance-cancel: the statement and form are in the contract only for insurance-paid jobs; the builder cannot tell whether a job is insurance-paid.
The state file says roofing contracts must show the Illinois roofing license name and number (513/18(d)); the license field was left unchanged because it is roofing only.
